rag_summary_count_consistency.details: The six identified_occurrences have six distinct occurrence IDs and agree with identified_bias_summary: one each for anchoring bias, availability heuristic, bandwagon effect, confirmation bias, psychological reactance, and sunk cost fallacy. candidate_biases is empty and no_supported_biases_found is false.

evaluation_limitations: The supplied RAG output claims retrieved corpus support, but no independent retrieved chunks or retrieval logs were supplied; corpus fidelity therefore cannot be scored.

The RAG labels availability heuristic and sunk cost fallacy are close to, but not exact matches for, the hidden Negativity Bias and Irrational Escalation labels; mechanism-first scoring is reported separately.
The hidden segment map is authoritative, so no additional neutral or negative reasoning segments are introduced.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Vendor rough estimate submitted as the working budget baseline; later internal estimate was framed as a 40% overrun.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant adopted an early externally supplied numeric estimate before detailed scoping and continued to frame later budget information relative to it.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Mixed usability results: six of ten users were confused, but the participant searched for positive comments and reframed confusion as an onboarding gap.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: The participant selectively retrieved favorable usability evidence supporting a navigation model they had designed and applied asymmetric scrutiny to negative evidence.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Microservices recommendation cited three peer firms; a single visible demo crash received more narrative weight than the 92% pilot success rate.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Peer adoption independently supported the architecture recommendation, while one salient negative incident outweighed aggregate positive outcome data in the risk narrative.

segments.speaker: Participant
segments.raw_interview_anchor: Despite delays and outages, migration continued because reverting would waste completed work; an authentication alternative was drafted mainly because the mandate was imposed.
segments.ground_truth_rationale: Continuation was justified by already-invested migration work rather than a rigorous forward-looking comparison, and pushback on authentication was driven primarily by the directive's imposed nature.

segment_level_adjudications.adjudication_note: The identified anchoring occurrence is high confidence, correctly localized, and matches the hidden mechanism and label.

segment_level_adjudications.localization_basis: obs_002 quotes the search for positive usability comments and the asymmetric treatment of confusion in the usability-results episode.
segment_level_adjudications.adjudication_note: The identified confirmation-bias occurrence is high confidence, correctly localized, and matches the hidden mechanism and label.

segment_level_adjudications.localization_basis: obs_003 uses the peer-firm architecture case studies and obs_004 uses the visible crash versus 92% pilot metric, both within the architecture/risk episode.
segment_level_adjudications.adjudication_note: The segment is detected at every threshold because obs_004 is high confidence. Instance-level strict scoring differs: obs_003 is an approved equivalent for Herding, while obs_004 captures the Negativity Bias mechanism under a near-neighbor label.

segment_level_adjudications.localization_basis: obs_005 quotes the directive-driven authentication response and obs_006 quotes continuation justified by already-invested migration work; both localize to the fourth decision point.
segment_level_adjudications.adjudication_note: Neither occurrence qualifies at high_only because both are moderate confidence. At higher thresholds, the segment is detected; obs_005 is an approved Reactance equivalent and obs_006 is a near-neighbor label with a full mechanism match.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Adoption of an early externally supplied vendor quote as a persistent budget baseline despite later, more accurate estimates.

instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support the budget-baseline mechanism.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Interpretation and communication of usability test results
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Selective retrieval of favorable usability-test comments and reframing of majority negative feedback as an onboarding issue, without equivalent scrutiny applied to positive feedback.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: The predicted label directly names the hidden target construct.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding captures favorable quote-seeking, mitigating explanations for negative evidence, and asymmetric scrutiny of the navigation test results.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support selective evidence retrieval and weighting.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Architecture decision between monolith refactor and microservices
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Justifying an architecture recommendation partly by peer-company adoption trends independent of internal technical risk assessment.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Bandwagon effect is an established equivalent/near-synonymous label for herding when the mechanism is adoption justified by others' adoption; the supplied mechanism fully matches.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding distinguishes peer-company adoption from the internal risk memo and describes peer success as making microservices feel validated.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support peer-adoption influence.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Decision to continue migration after delays and outages
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Continued commitment of resources to the migration justified by sunk/already-completed cutover work rather than forward-looking reassessment amid delays and outages.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Sunk cost fallacy is a close neighboring construct and a mechanism underlying escalation of commitment, but it is not treated as an approved alternate name for the hidden Irrational Escalation target.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures continuation driven by already-invested work and the failure to rigorously compare future costs and risks; its label foregrounds the sunk-cost mechanism rather than the broader escalation construct.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support the continuation rationale.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_decision_or_episode: Risk assessment framing after live demo crash
instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: A single salient negative demo event overriding a 92% aggregate success metric in the executive-facing risk narrative.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Availability heuristic is a near-neighbor explanation for overweighting an easily recalled vivid event, but it is not an approved alternate name for Negativity Bias.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding fully captures the single visible crash receiving disproportionate risk-narrative weight over the 92% success rate; the label emphasizes recall accessibility rather than the negative valence of the event.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support disproportionate weighting of the crash.

instance_level_adjudications.hidden_mechanism: Resistance to the security team's mandated authentication architecture driven primarily by its imposed nature rather than a distinct technical objection.
instance_level_adjudications.label_equivalence_explanation: Psychological reactance is the established scholarly form of the hidden Reactance label, and the stated mechanism matches.
instance_level_adjudications.mechanism_overlap_explanation: The finding identifies frustration at the directive, control preservation as the motivation for the alternative, and the absence of a substantive technical objection.
instance_level_adjudications.evidence_fidelity_assessment: Quotes are valid, attributed to the Participant, and directly support directive-triggered pushback.

unmatched_rag_predictions.why_not_an_exact_strict_match: The quote and mechanism exactly localize and explain the hidden event-weighting distortion, but availability heuristic is not the hidden Negativity Bias label or an approved alias. It is therefore a strict false positive while serving as a mechanism-first match.

The finding correctly captures the sunk-work rationale for continuing, but sunk cost fallacy is treated as a neighboring mechanism rather than an approved alternate name for the hidden Irrational Escalation label.

high_only.detection_interpretation: Three of four positive segments have a high-confidence detection; the fourth segment is missed because both of its findings are moderate confidence.

high_and_moderate.detection_interpretation: All four positive segments are detected once moderate-confidence findings are included.

all_identified_confidence_levels.detection_interpretation: All four positive segments are detected; adding the low-confidence herding finding does not change segment-level detection.

all_confidence_and_candidates.detection_interpretation: No candidates were supplied, so this threshold is identical to all_identified_confidence_levels.

rag_label_false_positive_inventory.mechanism_overlap_summary: Full overlap with the hidden salient-negative-event-overweighting mechanism; the label emphasizes mental availability rather than negative valence.
Full overlap with the hidden already-invested-work continuation mechanism; the label names the sunk-cost driver rather than the broader escalation construct.

corpus_support_audit.assessment_note: obs_001 and obs_002 explicitly claim retrieved support and include corpus evidence, while obs_003 through obs_006 disclose that retrieved support was unavailable. The two claimed citations have null source_identifier fields and no independent retrieved material or logs were supplied, so their provenance is unverifiable; this does not alter detection or classification scores.

confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_to_high_and_moderate: Segment F1 rises from 0.8571 to 1.0000; strict instance F1 rises from 0.4444 to 0.5455; mechanism-first instance F1 rises from 0.6667 to 0.9091.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_high_and_moderate_to_all_: Segment F1 is unchanged at 1.0000; strict instance F1 rises from 0.5455 to 0.6667 because the low-confidence Herding finding is admitted; mechanism-first instance F1 rises from 0.9091 to 1.0000.
confidence_tradeoff.increment_from_all_confidence_to_all_con: No change: the RAG output contains zero candidates.

overall_evaluation_summary.segment_level_primary_result: At the recommended high_and_moderate threshold, all 4 of 4 positive reasoning segments are detected with no false alarms in the supplied map; high_only detects 3 of 4.
overall_evaluation_summary.strict_label_plus_mechanism_result: At high_and_moderate and higher thresholds, 3 of 6 hidden instances are strict true positives; the other two identified findings are correctly localized but use near-neighbor labels, and Herding is recovered only when its low-confidence finding is included.
overall_evaluation_summary.mechanism_first_result: At high_and_moderate, 5 of 6 hidden mechanisms are recovered with no false positives; at all identified confidence levels, all 6 are recovered.
overall_evaluation_summary.candidate_tier_value_assessment: No candidates were supplied, so the candidate tier adds no detections, errors, or metric changes.
main_failure_modes: Two correct mechanisms were assigned near-neighbor labels rather than the hidden benchmark labels: availability heuristic for Negativity Bias and sunk cost fallacy for Irrational Escalation.
The Herding finding was assigned low confidence, causing it to be absent from the high-only and high-and-moderate instance scorecards.
main_strengths: All six identified findings are grounded in valid, directly relevant interview quotations.
All six findings localize to the correct positive segments and capture the intended mechanisms.
Anchoring Bias, Confirmation Bias, Herding, and Reactance are labeled exactly or with approved equivalents.
overall_evaluation_summary.benchmark_interpretation: This run has perfect segment-level detection once moderate confidence is admitted and perfect mechanism-first instance recovery once low confidence is admitted. The gap between mechanism-first and strict scores is entirely taxonomy-related: two near-neighbor labels are not accepted as strict target labels.
